reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since the handoff from W2 is only a claim. I'll start by listing the orders.
Orders are listed, but I should also check the refunds list to verify W2's claim before any payouts are recorded, since payouts can't be recalled.
The refunds match W2's handoff and each refund maps to an order I can see. Per the task, I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355, which matches orders 290 and 293 (4834 + 35521 = 40355) with no refunds against acme. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40935 matches orders 291 and 294 (36109 + 15074 = 51183) minus the 10248 refund on order 294. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net of 25715 matches orders 292 and 295 (9909 + 27790 = 37699) minus refunds 2929 and 9055 (11984), so all three balances reconcile with the orders and refunds. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 40355 is recorded and matches its orders. Birch's balance of 40935 reconciles with orders 291 and 294 less the refund on 294, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 40935 is recorded. Cobalt's balance of 25715 reconciles with orders 292 and 295 less refunds 2929 and 9055, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded, and each matches the orders and refunds I checked: acme 40355, birch 40935, cobalt 25715. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
